A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths that enable individuals and groups to thrive.

positive psychology has the potential to reorient psychology and psychiatry from a preoccupation with repairing and correcting what is wrong to a new science and practice focused on what goes right in human beings.
positive psychology has three central concerns: positive emotions, positive individual traits, and positive institutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
positive psychology is not about feeling good. Rather, it is about how to lead a good life, a flourishing life.
human strengths can be cultivated and that this is a necessary complement to the focus on human weakness that has been the hallmark of modern psychology.
positive traits, positive states, and positive activities are not simply the absence of negative traits and states but rather represent a set of phenomena in their own right.
